targets.authors: Woltin, K.-A., Corneille, O., Yzerbyt, V. Y., & Förster, J.
targets.title: Narrowing down to open up for other people’s concerns: Empathic concern can be enhanced by inducing detailed processing.
targets.evidence_quote: The current project was an attempted replication of Woltin et al. (2011). In their original study, the authors found that priming low-power concepts resulted in greater self-reported empathic concern than priming high-power concepts.
targets.outcome_quote: The final (Stage 2) sample for the replication consisted of 265 total participants (136 in the powerful condition, 129 in the powerless condition, thus meeting our preregistered sample size of 126 per experimental group). No statistically significant difference between the two conditions was found, F(1, 263) = 0.757, p = .385, Cohen’s d = 0.11. Again, mean ECS score for the powerful group (M = 3.21, SD = 0.40) were descriptively larger compared to the powerless group (M = 3.17, SD = 0.36).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The specified original low-power advantage was absent and descriptive means were reversed in both stages; the reported pooled Bayesian analysis supports the null.
